blocks.en:
• 25 mrad. Agreement is 13.7 pm overall and 9.0 pm on the 16 columns farthest from the edge of the free-atom box (111 of the 127 lie within 3 Å of it in a 13.3 Å field). The difference is 10 times the combined standard deviation. The two starts of our fit agree to 0.05 pm rms on the in-box atoms, so the difference from the published peaks is model or readout error. The position bars at one optimum are therefore not a credible interval for positions on these data.
The width bars stand as in §§S3–S4. • Public. Agreement is 14 pm in the interior and 26.7 pm in the outer 3 Å, where our fitted sub-scan ends. • 6 ∘ bilayer. Our atoms agree with the published phase worse than the ideal two-lattice start does (32 against 18 pm). The fit moves the atoms by 42–49 pm in random directions, its coherence parameters sit at their bounds ( σ f \sigma_{f} = 120 Å, σ src \sigma_{\mathrm{src}} = 0.5 Å), and it trails the published reconstruction by 0.09 per pixel in D H D_{H} (§S10). The positions absorb instrument mismatch and are not accurate. • Where the two differ. At the edges of the fitted field, at overlapping columns (25 mrad: 17.1 against 12.3 pm on isolated columns), and at low-amplitude Se 2 columns, 5–6% of them, about the fraction of Se vacancies in [ 22 ] . Our full-occupancy model does not widen those sites ( U a \sqrt{U_{a}} of Se 6.1 against 6.6 pm elsewhere on the 6 ∘ bilayer). These sites need an occupancy parameter. On real data and an independent simulator, model error, not counting noise, sets both methods’ position error: 14–19 pm on real data ( 0.08 ​ λ / α 0.08\,\lambda/\alpha ), about 10 times our Fisher bars.

Every column over every training pattern of the 25 mrad sub-scan (1,636 columns, 896 patterns) costs about 390 CPU node-hours or 75 A100-hours (0.18 s per column and pattern). A field the size of the 6 ∘ bilayer (14,336 patterns, 9,458 parameters) would cost about 6,800 A100-hours.
Local assembly fails. Width columns of fixed atoms outside the 13.3 Å scan draw information from the whole sub-scan through the 25 Å probe window. Truncating them changes the width bars by a median of 33% (p90 183%) at a 5 Å footprint, 3.4% (44%) at 6 Å and 1.1% (23%) at 8 Å. The dense matrix is therefore formed. Its factorization takes seconds on a GPU.

About 70% of a patch’s columns are per-pattern scan offsets. A low-dose scan can replace them with a cubic scan model (18 columns), freeze calibrated parameters, and take the instrument, including the second-order aberrations 𝐀 2 \mathbf{A}_{2} and 𝐁 2 \mathbf{B}_{2} , and the widths from a high-dose calibration. The target scan then refits positions, the interlayer distance, defocus C 1 C_{1} , two-fold astigmatism 𝐀 1 \mathbf{A}_{1} , dose scale, background and descan. One Gaussian position jitter, a free log ⁡ σ src \log\sigma_{\mathrm{src}} , catches the scan’s blur. Each row adds to the one above. The last row is the alternative in which coma is refit: design n n passes rank, 100 e/Å 2 D D , W / Se (e/Å 2 ) variance, W / Se all profiled (species widths) 1,084–1,104 342–358 87–89% 193–206 / 657–1,076 1 / 1 scan model 358–374 342–358 62–67% 173–185 / 622–1,058 0.90 / 0.97 + calibration and jitter ( Fig. 6 ) 349–365 333–349 62–67% 110–122 / 540–995 0.58 / 0.88 + C 1 C_{1} and 𝐀 1 \mathbf{A}_{1} also held 342–358 326–342 61–66% 110–122 / 535–993 0.58 / 0.87 𝐀 2 \mathbf{A}_{2} , 𝐁 2 \mathbf{B}_{2} refit 353–369 337–353 62–67% 173–184 / 616–1,057 0.90 / 0.97 D D is the dose at which the core W or Se position reaches 0.1 ​ λ / α 0.1\,\lambda/\alpha with every other estimated parameter profiled; the pivot-conditional D k D_{k} does not change (61–94 and 440–980 e/Å 2 ). Variance is relative to the profiled design (median over the core coordinates). The design of Fig. 6 estimates 3.02–3.11 times fewer parameters. The passes barely change: the offsets take two passes in any design, and one width per species adds only two columns. At 100 e/Å 2 every core position stays determined, and the position bounds tighten by 24% (W) and 6% (Se). The jitter leaves them unchanged and is determined to 12% (relative standard deviation of the total Gaussian spread, 0.32 Å). Holding C 1 C_{1} and 𝐀 1 \mathbf{A}_{1} as well changes little (24% and 7%).
The gain comes from the axial coma 𝐁 2 \mathbf{B}_{2} , which trades with in-plane position. Holding 𝐁 2 \mathbf{B}_{2} alone gives the same 24% and 6%, and 𝐀 2 \mathbf{A}_{2} does not matter. If coma must be refit, the bounds tighten by only 5% and 2%. Holding it is valid when coma drifts by much less than the target scan can resolve. The target scan alone pins 𝐁 2 \mathbf{B}_{2} only to about 30 nm at 100 e/Å 2 (0.4 nm at the dataset dose), and a coma error of that size biases the positions by about half a standard deviation. Coma drift is negligible between scans taken minutes apart and reaches about 20 nm over an hour, a bias of a third of a standard deviation. The calibration scan is therefore taken next to the target in time as well as in space. Defocus and two-fold astigmatism drift in minutes and are refit [ 3 ] .

blocks.en: Two later scans of the same session are fitted with the same pipeline. One is taken 70 min after the first at the same magnification and dose. The other is taken 83 min after it at 10 instead of 14.5 Mx and half the dose. We express each change of a calibrated parameter in units of its low-dose threshold, the Fisher standard deviation of the first scan scaled to 100 e/Å 2 . The slow aberrations that the design holds fixed transfer on both scans within one threshold: 𝐁 2 \mathbf{B}_{2} changes by at most 0.01, 𝐀 2 \mathbf{A}_{2} by at most 0.92, C s C_{s} by at most 0.11 and α \alpha by at most 0.30. The terms it refits move, as the design assumes: defocus by 2.0 and 2.1 thresholds, 𝐀 1 \mathbf{A}_{1} by up to 4.5, and the descan by up to 6.4. The coherence widths stay inside one threshold at the same magnification, the focal spread changing by 0.52 and the source size by 0.10. On the 10 Mx scan they move by 1.15 (71 to 83 Å) and 1.86 (0.32 to 0.38 Å). The design holds the focal spread fixed, and its jitter term adds to the source size. The species widths are 7.78 and 10.18 pm at the same magnification, close to the 7.35 and 8.98 pm of the first scan. The 10 Mx scan fits 14.4 and 11.6 pm, so part of its coherence change may be blur that the widths absorb. Within a session, the coherence widths therefore transfer to within one or two thresholds.
blocks.zh: 同一会话的后两次扫描装有同一种管线. 一个在第一个之后70分钟 在同一放大和剂量。 另一种是在10分之后取出83分,而不是14.5Mx和剂量的一半. 我们用其低剂量阈值的单位表示一个校正参数的每个变化,第一次扫描的费舍尔标准偏差缩放为100 e/ à 2。 设计在两个扫描上进行固定转移的缓慢异常: B 2\ mathbf{B}_{2} 变化最多为 0.01, A 2\mathbf{A}_{2} 变化最多为 0.92, C s C_{s} 变化最多为 0.11, α\ alpha 变化最多为 0.30. 它所移动的术语,如设计假设:以2.0和2.1的阈值去聚焦,以A 1\ mathbf{A}_{1}去至4.5;以去色能去至6.4. 一致性宽度在同一放大时会停留在一个阈值之内,焦距会变化0.52,源大小会变化0.10. 在10次Mx扫描中,它们以1.15(71至83)和1.86(0.32至0.38)移动。 设计将焦距固定,它的焦距会增加出源大小. 物种宽度为7.78平方公尺和10.18平方公尺同为放大平方公尺,接近于第一次扫描的7.35平方公尺和8.98平方公尺. 10Mx扫描符合14.4和11.6pm,因此其部分一致性变化可能模糊到宽度被吸收. 在会期内,一致性宽度因此转移到一两个阈值之内。

blocks.en: 1. Initialize detector and scan parameters from a pixel fit with the same instrument model. Atoms start from the lattice, widths from a shared value per species. 2. Adam on mini-batches of 32–512 training positions with a cosine learning-rate schedule (60 epochs by default), for fits from a coarse start; refits from a converged fit go straight to the polish. Loss: Eq. 7 over T T and the detector pixels inside the band-limited disc, plus Gaussian priors (atom displacements 0.3 Å; scan polynomial; the aberrations 𝐀 1 \mathbf{A}_{1} , 𝐀 2 \mathbf{A}_{2} , 𝐁 2 \mathbf{B}_{2} and C s C_{s} , with none on the defocus; log ⁡ σ f \log\sigma_{f} , log ⁡ σ src \log\sigma_{\mathrm{src}} ), and offsets | 𝜹 j | ≤ 1 |\boldsymbol{\delta}_{j}|\leq 1 Å. Cost per epoch: one forward and one reverse pass over T T , about twice step (a). 3. Polish: full-batch L-BFGS with a strong-Wolfe line search (history 20), in blocks of 5 iterations and segments of 20. On real data every parameter is scaled by its Fisher standard deviation from a dense K = 8 K=8 Fisher matrix computed once at an earlier nearby fit; the simulated-bilayer fits scale each parameter group by a fixed constant. Up to three polish rounds are run. The probe-mode basis is frozen within a round and refreshed between rounds, until a refresh changes the objective by less than 1 nat. Stop when the squared Newton decrement 𝐠 ⊤ ​ ℐ − 1 ​ 𝐠 \mathbf{g}^{\!\top}\mathcal{I}^{-1}\mathbf{g} is below 0.1 and every step is below 0.1 Fisher standard deviations, both on training patterns only. Here 𝐠 \mathbf{g} includes the priors and ℐ \mathcal{I} the prior precision. One start meets this rule (0.006, largest step 0.04 sd). The other ends at 0.18, with its largest steps 0.38 and 0.34 sd in log ⁡ σ src \log\sigma_{\mathrm{src}} and log ⁡ σ f \log\sigma_{f} and at most 0.04 sd in any atom parameter. Its positions and widths are converged; its coherence widths are not. 4. Label exchanges. Two atoms of one species whose projected positions coincide share a column, and only the weak depth contrast of the multislice decides which layer holds which. A continuous optimizer cannot swap them: the straight path passes through the coincident configuration. The exchange screen evaluates every such swap from the current point on the training patterns near the column (one frozen probe basis, the same frozen-phonon draws before and after) and accepts improving swaps with disjoint pattern sets. An accepted set is kept only if the full training objective drops by more than a threshold per swap, both at the fitting configurations and at a phonon seed never used for scoring. The relaxed exchange test imposes a candidate swap and refits from it, keeping the swap if the refit ends lower. 5. Numerics: the slice loop is checkpointed, so memory is that of one slice per mode and position plus the stored slice boundaries. Waves are single-precision complex, and the likelihood is accumulated in double precision. Double precision throughout is an option, used for derivative checks. Fit state is checkpointed for restart.

blocks.en: The parameters split into groups that a measurement determines at different doses (§S16). The instrument (aberrations, coherence, aperture, detector) and the thermal widths need a high dose, the atom positions a low one. 1. Calibrate: fit everything, steps (a)–(b), on a high-dose scan of an area next to the target, or of a radiation-hard specimen at the same imaging conditions. The gun (source size, energy spread), the detector, the aperture, C s C_{s} and the second-order aberrations 𝐀 2 \mathbf{A}_{2} and 𝐁 2 \mathbf{B}_{2} transfer while the corrector is not retuned; on a second scan of the same session the coherence widths hold only to one or two low-dose thresholds (§S16). Coma drifts negligibly over minutes and by up to about 20 nm in an hour [ 3 ] . Defocus and two-fold astigmatism 𝐀 1 \mathbf{A}_{1} drift in minutes and are refit on the target, with tilt, thickness, dose scale, background and descan. The thermal widths, a property of the material, come from a prior fit, tables or simulation. Repeating the calibration scan after the target bounds the drift. 2. Image: scan the target at low dose and fit only the positions, a smooth scan model, and the drifting terms of step 1, steps (a)–(b), with the calibrated parameters held fixed except one Gaussian position jitter. A Gaussian spread of probe positions adds to σ src \sigma_{\mathrm{src}} in quadrature. With the instrument calibration transferred, this one per-scan term catches session blur (stage vibration, drift jitter) that would otherwise widen every atom. It acts on the probe, so unlike a blur of the potential it is not degenerate with the mean of the per-atom widths. 3. Bound: compute the error bars of the positions, step (d), with the fixed parameters as known, and the bias a calibration error would cause. A pixel reconstruction estimates every pixel of the object and the probe from the low-dose counts; here they determine about three numbers per atom. The bounds assume the model is right; experiments at these doses are the test.

blocks.en:
The solver has three parts: Adam on mini-batches, a full-batch L-BFGS polish, and the scaling of parameters in that polish. On the simulated bilayer the ablation holds the model, data, start and held-out set fixed and changes only the optimizer: Adam alone for the same wall time; Adam then L-BFGS in raw units; and the production solver (Adam, then L-BFGS with per-group scales). Each arm is scored by training objective, held-out D H D_{H} and error against truth, against wall time.
Two effects are already measured. On real data, Fisher scaling decides whether per-atom widths move at all: unscaled, L-BFGS leaves 98% of the 1,702 widths within 1% of their start after 400 iterations; scaled, 66% of the interior widths move within 40 iterations and the held-out deviance falls (§S3). On the simulated bilayer, 10 Adam epochs (1.96 h) reach 3.3 pm in-plane but leave depth near its start, and the full-batch polish moves each atom toward its likelihood minimum in depth (§§S6, S11).

已经测量出两种效果。 在真实数据上,费舍尔缩放决定了每个原子的宽度是否完全移动:未缩放,L-BFGS在400个迭代之后的1 702个宽度的1%范围内留下了98%;缩放,66%的内部宽度在40个迭代之内移动并被扣出偏离(§S3)。 在模拟的双层层上,10个亚当纪元(1.96 h)在飞机上达到3.3平方米,但在起跑点附近留下了深度,而满分光圈将每个原子向最小概率的深度移动(XXS6,S11)。

blocks.en: S18. Exact Foldy–Lax reference
blocks.zh: S18. 准确的Foldy - Lax 参考文献

blocks.en:
The reference is Foldy–Lax multiple scattering with partial-wave T-matrices. Each atom carries the thermally smeared Peng potential of Eq. 9 , tapered to zero at 7 Å, in the relativistically corrected scalar wave equation. Its phase shifts δ l \delta_{l} come from the variable-phase equation (fourth-order Runge–Kutta), giving a T-matrix diagonal in l l , T l = ( e 2 ​ i ​ δ l − 1 ) / 2 T_{l}=(e^{2i\delta_{l}}-1)/2 . The optical theorem holds to nine digits, and ELSEPA [ 55 ] agrees on the same potential to 3.6 × 10 − 4 3.6\times 10^{-4} in the dark field. Foldy–Lax [ 15 , 30 ] then makes the wave incident on each atom of a column the beam plus the outgoing waves of all others, coupled by outgoing-to-regular translations.
GMRES, preconditioned by the forward-only sweep, solves it to a residual of 10 − 12 10^{-12} in 0–36 iterations; dense LU agrees to 2 × 10 − 15 2\times 10^{-15} .

blocks.en: Limitations (full list)
blocks.zh: 限制(完整名单)

blocks.en: • Bounds assume the model is right. Thermal diffuse scattering and partial coherence are the remaining model errors. • Fits are slower than a learned network (minutes against seconds). The learned output is a good warm start. • The detector blur σ d 2 \sigma_{d}^{2} of Tab. S1 is an effective blur. On specimen data it can also absorb small-angle inelastic scattering, which the model omits. • Se bounds assume full occupancy. About 5% of Se sites are vacant in these samples, beam-induced at 80 kV and confined to the outer Se planes [ 22 ] . A vacancy trades against a wider Se site, so Se widths need an occupancy parameter per site (W unaffected). • Ellipse (anisotropy) bounds assume a rigid scan and a flat layer. Drift is about 1 Å per minute, i.e . 0.3 Å over a 16 s scan (0.5% of the field), and moiré corrugations bend each layer [ 22 ] . Both can mimic anisotropy. Per-region tilt and drift parameters would absorb both and are not fitted here. • Per-site widths on the public 10.3 mrad data are effective column widths. The W and Se 2 sublattices are not told apart, and pairs closer than 0.4 Å merge into one column. • The simulated benchmark is static and coherent. It tests positions and the instrument model, not thermal widths, which are checked against molecular dynamics and thermometry. • Atoms are fitted only in a thin specimen (0.15 depths of field). The thick specimens (PdH, PrScO 3 , PZT, 4.9–12.8 depths of field) are fitted with a pixel object. Thick specimens matter: specimens cut from bulk are tens of nanometers thick, and there multislice ptychography reached the lattice-vibration limit [ 6 ] . Atoms are harder there: a column holds tens of atoms, the wave channels along it, and its atoms lie ten times closer in depth than the depth of field (3.95 against 41 Å for PZT), so the counts barely fix one atom’s depth. A column must then be parameterized jointly, e.g . as a lattice with displacements.

blocks.en: Bounds assume the model is right. Thermal diffuse scattering and partial coherence are the remaining model errors.
blocks.zh: 假设模型是正确的 其余的模型错误是热散射和部分一致性。

blocks.en: Se bounds assume full occupancy. About 5% of Se sites are vacant in these samples, beam-induced at 80 kV and confined to the outer Se planes [ 22 ] . A vacancy trades against a wider Se site, so Se widths need an occupancy parameter per site (W unaffected).

blocks.en: Ellipse (anisotropy) bounds assume a rigid scan and a flat layer. Drift is about 1 Å per minute, i.e . 0.3 Å over a 16 s scan (0.5% of the field), and moiré corrugations bend each layer [ 22 ] . Both can mimic anisotropy. Per-region tilt and drift parameters would absorb both and are not fitted here.
